newsitem.title: USA: Nichols says weeping prosecutors should be barred.
newsitem.headline: Nichols says weeping prosecutors should be barred.

text.p: Federal prosecutors from Oklahoma City should be barred from Terry Nichols' trial because they cried in front of jurors during the first bombing trial, Nichols' lawyers said Tuesday.
Nichols is scheduled to go on trial Sept. 29 for the April 19, 1995 bombing the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City that killed 168.
Nichols' co-defendant Timothy McVeigh was convicted and sentenced to death last month.
During the first bombing trial the judge had to admonish Patrick Ryan, the U.S. attorney in Oklahoma City, against "crying in front of the jury," according to newly released court filings.

The Justice Department said the request should be denied, but admitted "it was unwise, given the emotional toll of preparing and presenting the testimony," to assign certain courtroom work to Oklahoma City prosecutors.

"The burden of presenting victim-witnesses at (Nichols') trial will more evenly be distributed among all members of the prosecution team ...," Justice Department prosecutors told U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch in a filing.
The two U.S. prosecutors from Oklahoma City at McVeigh's trial, Ryan and Vicki Behenna, were noticably emotional on several occasions during heart-wrenching testimony about the effect of the blast.
According to the transcript, the judge said the emotion of the proseuctors "certainly ... is understandable; but I can't have counsel crying in front of the jury."
